title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZS (Re-conversion of Producer Company to inter-State co-operative society)

content.overview: Section 378ZS provides a route for an erstwhile inter-State co-operative society that became a Producer Company under Chapter XXIA to apply to the Tribunal for re-conversion. The section specifies qualifying member or creditor support, a Tribunal-directed meeting, voting thresholds and disclosure of material facts before sanction.
content.glance: Re-conversion under section 378ZS requires the statutory application route, member/creditor thresholds, a Tribunal-directed meeting, the required vote, Tribunal sanction and disclosure of material facts.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZS (Re-conversion of Producer Company to inter-State co-operative society). An erstwhile inter-State co-operative society registered as a Producer Company under Chapter XXIA may apply to the Tribunal after a general-meeting resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of Members present and voting, or on request by creditors representing three-fourths in value of total creditors. The Tribunal directs a meeting. The section sets a further majority-in-number and three-fourths-in-value threshold among Members or creditors present and voting in person, as applicable. Before sanction, the Tribunal must be satisfied that all material facts have been disclosed, including the latest financial position, latest auditor report and pending Chapter XIV investigation proceedings. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Application route
sections.body: An eligible Producer Company that was formerly an inter-State co-operative society may apply to the Tribunal after a general-meeting resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of Members present and voting, or on request by creditors representing three-fourths in value of its total creditors.

sections.heading: Tribunal-directed meeting and vote
sections.body: The Tribunal directs a meeting of Members or creditors, as applicable. The section requires a majority in number representing three-fourths in value of the Members or creditors, as applicable, present and voting in person to agree to re-conversion, subject to Tribunal sanction.

sections.heading: Disclosure before sanction
sections.body: The Tribunal must not sanction re-conversion unless satisfied that the applicant has disclosed all material facts, including the latest financial position, the latest auditor report on the accounts and pending investigation proceedings in relation to the company under Chapter XIV.

sections.heading: Scope note
sections.body: Apply the exact statutory route and voting test to the relevant category of applicant and meeting. Do not treat a proposal, resolution or creditor request alone as completing re-conversion; Tribunal sanction and the section's disclosure condition remain material.

examples.title: Checking a proposed re-conversion
examples.body: Check whether the applicant is an erstwhile inter-State co-operative society registered as a Producer Company under Chapter XXIA; identify the applicable member-resolution or creditor-request route; verify the Tribunal-directed meeting and vote; and confirm disclosure of material facts before Tribunal sanction.

hypotheticals.question: A Producer Company seeks re-conversion to an inter-State co-operative society. Which statutory checks arise under section 378ZS?
hypotheticals.analysis: Confirm the eligibility described by the section; identify whether the application follows the Members' resolution route or the qualifying creditors' request route; check the Tribunal-directed meeting and the applicable voting threshold; and assess whether all material facts specified by the section have been disclosed before sanction. Do not assume approval from the initial resolution or request alone.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a general-meeting resolution or creditor request as sufficient by itself to complete re-conversion.
misconceptions.correction: Section 378ZS also provides for a Tribunal-directed meeting, the applicable vote and Tribunal sanction.

misconceptions.trap: Applying the same threshold without checking whether the relevant route concerns Members or creditors.
misconceptions.correction: Identify the applicant route and apply the specific member or creditor tests stated in the section.

misconceptions.trap: Overlooking disclosure of material facts before Tribunal sanction.
misconceptions.correction: Check disclosure of the latest financial position, latest auditor report and pending Chapter XIV investigation proceedings, as identified by the section.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zs do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A Producer Company that was formerly an inter-State co-operative society may apply to the Tribunal for re-conversion, subject to the voting, creditor and filing requirements in the section.
